name: Measure investment risk and monitor limits each business day
summary: Every business day the portfolio risk team turns the previous day's positions, prices and benchmarks into risk numbers for each pool and client portfolio (active risk, value at risk, factor and currency exposures, leverage and liquidity) and checks them against board limits and each client's policy ranges. Most of the morning goes to fixing data: new securities without a risk mapping, stale prices, proxies for private holdings and position breaks. Warnings go to portfolio managers; breaches are escalated through the director to the chief investment officer, cured by trades or formally excepted, and reported to clients or the board when needed. The daily report usually goes out by mid-morning, but limits held in spreadsheets, proxy-based private asset risk and value at risk measures that miss tail risk are known weak points.

baseline.org_archetype: A provincial not-for-profit asset manager with about 240 staff and $79 billion under management for four public sector clients (five portfolios) and four pools, with an 18-person risk division.
baseline.notes: Unit of work is one business day's risk run across all pools and client portfolios. Volumes and staffing follow the org file: about 21 runs a month and nine people in portfolio risk.

trigger: The investment book of record closes the business day and end-of-day positions, prices and benchmark data become available for the overnight risk batch.
end_state: The daily risk report is published to the CIO and portfolio managers, every warning is logged and notified, and any breach has been cured or formally excepted and reported to the client or board where required.

volume.seasonality: One run per business day; volatile markets (for example March 2020) raise warnings, breaches and data exceptions, and month and quarter ends add private asset value updates to the proxies.

evidence.note: Business days per month, as in the org file's business_days driver.

Five analysts in the org file; two are on the morning run on any day, including time answering portfolio managers' questions on the numbers, and the rest of their time goes to monthly reporting, stress tests and ad hoc analysis. Cost from the org file (above the NOC 11101 Toronto median for quantitative specialists, loaded 1.35).
Three senior managers review the daily report in rotation and own limit events.
Escalates hard breaches; a few hours a month.
Concurs with exceptions and informs the board committee; independent channel to the board is FSRA leading practice.
Decides remediation or seeks an exception for breaches of board limits.

roles.title: Portfolio manager, total portfolio (rebalancing, liquidity, overlays)

evidence.note: Total portfolio managers execute rebalancing or overlay trades to cure breaches; other portfolio managers do the same for strategy limits.
Investment data analysts correct security master, price and position feed errors raised by the risk team.

roles.title: Client relationship manager (lead for one or two clients)

evidence.note: Tells the client about a breach of its policy ranges and the plan to cure it.

systems.name: Order management, pre-trade compliance and investment book of record platform (vendor software as a service)
Investment data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Market data terminals and vendor feeds (prices, indices, reference data)
Risk analytics system (third-party factor and stress models)
Email, video calls and collaboration suite

steps.name: Load end-of-day positions, prices and benchmarks
steps.description: After the investment book of record closes the day, scheduled jobs extract positions and cash for every pool, client portfolio and external mandate, together with vendor prices, exchange rates, index constituents and the latest proxy values for private holdings, and load them into the risk system.

error.defect_description: A feed fails or loads partial data.

evidence.note: Daily aggregation of positions and exposures is described by a peer; batch timing after the book of record closes is an estimate.

steps.name: Run automated data checks and overnight risk calculations
steps.description: The risk system flags missing or stale prices, securities not mapped to the factor model, large day-over-day position changes and benchmark file gaps, then calculates active risk, value at risk, factor and currency exposures, leverage and liquidity for each pool and client portfolio.

next.condition: next morning is a business day
run falls before a weekend or holiday

evidence.note: Measures named in the client policy (total risk, tracking error, factor decomposition) and the vendor's value at risk and factor tools; the weekend share is about one day in five.

steps.name: Results wait over the weekend or holiday
steps.description: When the run falls on a Friday or before a statutory holiday, the overnight results and exception report sit unreviewed until the risk team returns on the next business day, unless a market event prompts someone to look in.

evidence.note: Calendar effect of a business-day process; holidays add a third day.

steps.name: Review the data quality exception report
steps.description: The analyst on the morning rotation opens the exception report, compares position totals with the book of record and the reconciliation status for each account, and decides which exceptions are cosmetic, which can be fixed in the risk system and which need corrected data from investment data management or operations.

error.defect_description: A material data problem is treated as cosmetic and flows into the results.

control.basis: The model manager risk data control standard: daily review of risk data completeness and accuracy before results are used

next.condition: exceptions fixable in the risk system
upstream price, security or position error

evidence.note: Exception mix is an estimate; new securities, derivatives and private asset proxies make clean days uncommon for a multi-asset fund.

steps.name: Fix security mappings, proxies and derivative terms
steps.description: The analyst maps new securities to the factor model, assigns a public market proxy to a new or revalued private holding, corrects the terms of a swap or option, or overrides a stale price with a documented alternative, keeping a log of each manual override.

error.defect_description: Wrong proxy or mapping chosen, distorting exposure for the holding.

evidence.note: Private holdings represented by public proxies, as the org file notes; times are estimates.

steps.name: Correct upstream price, security or position data
steps.description: An investment data analyst receives the risk team's email or ticket, fixes the security master record or price, or chases operations for a corrected position after a reconciliation break, and confirms when the corrected feed has been resent to the risk system.

error.defect_description: Correction applied to the wrong record.

evidence.note: Handoff to the investment data team is typical; queue time is an estimate.

steps.name: Rerun risk calculations for affected portfolios
steps.description: The risk system recalculates exposures and risk measures for the pools and portfolios touched by the corrections, which for large multi-asset portfolios with derivatives can take a noticeable part of the morning.

evidence.note: Rerun time is an estimate for a vendor system.

steps.name: Review risk results and day-over-day changes
steps.description: The analyst reads each pool's and client portfolio's active risk, value at risk, factor, currency and liquidity numbers against yesterday, ties large moves to trades, cash flows or market moves, and treats any move that has no business explanation as a possible data error.

error.defect_description: A data-driven jump is explained away as a market move.

next.condition: unexplained jump points to a data error

evidence.note: Daily review of exposures is described by a peer; measures follow the client policy. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Check limits and client policy ranges
steps.description: The analyst compares each measure with the board-approved limits and with every client's asset mix ranges and risk targets, held partly in the risk system and partly in a controlled spreadsheet, and highlights any measure above the warning threshold or outside a limit.

error.defect_description: A limit or range in the spreadsheet is out of date, so a breach is missed or a false breach raised.

control.basis: The model manager investment risk policy: board-approved limits on active risk, value at risk, leverage and liquidity, with breach escalation and remediation procedures; Client statements of investment policies and procedures: asset mix ranges, benchmarks and risk targets

evidence.note: Daily monitoring against limits and target allocations is stated by the model manager and peers; the flag rate across nine pools and portfolios is an estimate.

steps.name: Verify the flagged limit usage
steps.description: Before raising an alarm the analyst rechecks the positions, prices, benchmark weights, pending trades and expected cash flows behind the flagged measure and, where needed, asks the portfolio manager or operations whether a trade or cash movement explains it.

next.condition: caused by bad data, fix and rerun

evidence.note: False-flag share is an estimate.

steps.name: Assess the cause and classify the limit event
steps.description: The risk manager reviews the confirmed event, judges whether it is passive (market move, client cash flow) or active (a portfolio decision), classifies it as a warning or a breach under the policy, and sets the required action and date.

next.condition: breach of a board limit or client range

evidence.note: Breach treatment set in the risk policy; the warning to breach split is an estimate.

steps.name: Notify the portfolio manager of the near breach and log it
steps.description: The risk manager emails the responsible portfolio manager, the total portfolio team and the asset class head with the measure, the threshold and the date by which the position should be reviewed, and records the warning in the limit event register.

evidence.note: Typical warning practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Log the breach and notify the portfolio manager
steps.description: The risk manager records the breach, its cause, the required action and the cure date in the limit event register and calls and emails the portfolio manager and the head of the asset class or total portfolio management.

control.basis: The model manager investment risk policy: board-approved limits on active risk, value at risk, leverage and liquidity, with breach escalation and remediation procedures: breach logged with required action and date

evidence.note: Escalation and remediation procedures are required by peer policies.

steps.name: Escalate the breach to the CIO and chief risk officer
steps.description: The director of portfolio risk reviews the breach note and sends it to the chief investment officer and the chief risk officer with the recommended action, the cure date and whether a board or client notification will be needed.

control.basis: The model manager investment risk policy: board-approved limits on active risk, value at risk, leverage and liquidity, with breach escalation and remediation procedures: escalation of breaches to senior management

evidence.note: Late or incomplete escalation was a finding of the AIMCo review; independent channel to senior management is FSRA leading practice.

steps.name: Compile and publish the daily report with the breach section
steps.description: On a breach day the analyst builds the daily dashboard and report with a breach section showing the measure, limit, cause and required action, has the risk manager check that section, and sends it to the CIO, portfolio managers and the total portfolio team.

error.defect_description: Report figure differs from the risk system.

evidence.note: Breach-day reporting; runs alongside the escalation.

steps.name: Compile the daily risk report and dashboard
steps.description: The analyst refreshes the business intelligence dashboard, exports the summary tables for each pool and client portfolio, writes short commentary on the main changes and any warnings, and saves the report for review.

error.defect_description: Report figure differs from the risk system.

evidence.note: Automated report packages from the risk system plus manual commentary; times are estimates.

steps.name: Review the daily report before release
steps.description: A risk manager scans the draft for figures that look wrong, checks warnings against the register and the commentary against the numbers, and releases the report or sends it back for correction.

control.basis: The model manager risk reporting procedure: second-person review of risk reports before distribution

evidence.note: Four-eyes review is common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Publish the dashboard and email the report
steps.description: The reporting tool publishes the approved dashboard and emails the daily report to the CIO, asset class heads, portfolio managers and the total portfolio team, and stores it for the monthly risk report and the board risk committee.

evidence.note: Distribution step.

steps.name: CIO decides remediation or seeks an exception
steps.description: The chief investment officer reads the escalation memo, talks to the portfolio manager and decides whether to reduce the position within the cure period or to ask for a temporary exception, for example when a client cash flow or a private asset revaluation caused the breach.

control.basis: The model manager investment risk policy: board-approved limits on active risk, value at risk, leverage and liquidity, with breach escalation and remediation procedures: only the CIO may direct a cure or request an exception; variations outside board limits need prior board approval (peer practice)

evidence.note: Prior board approval for variations outside limits, with de minimis variances approved by the CEO, in a peer policy; exception share is an estimate.

steps.name: Execute remediation trades or overlay changes
steps.description: The total portfolio manager, or the strategy's portfolio manager, places futures, swaps or physical trades, or switches pool units, to bring the measure back inside the limit, and tells the risk team what was done.

error.defect_description: Trade sized too small to cure the breach.

evidence.note: Trades to bring exposures back in line are described by a peer and the client policy; times are estimates.

steps.name: Confirm the breach is cured in the following run
steps.description: In the next day's run the analyst checks the measure against the limit again and records whether the breach is cured or still open, re-escalating any breach that remains past its cure date.

evidence.note: Cure confirmation in the next run; still-open share is an estimate.

steps.name: Close the breach record and prepare notifications
steps.description: The risk manager closes the register entry with the cure date or the exception reference, drafts the summary for the monthly risk report and the board risk committee, and decides who outside the risk team must be told.

evidence.note: Risk exposures and breaches reported to the board at least quarterly; client reviews compliance quarterly. Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Chief risk officer concurs with a temporary exception
steps.description: The chief risk officer reviews the CIO's request, agrees or refuses a temporary exception with an expiry date and any conditions, and records it so the daily check shows the exception until it lapses.

control.basis: The model manager risk policy: exceptions require concurrence of the independent second line (chief risk officer), separate from the investment team

evidence.note: Independent risk function with a channel to senior management and the board; approver is an assumption.

steps.name: Tell the client about the policy range breach
steps.description: The client relationship manager calls or emails the client's investment staff to explain the breach of its asset mix range or risk target, the cause and the cure, and notes it for the client's quarterly compliance report.

control.basis: Client investment management agreement and statement of investment policies: notice of policy breaches and quarterly compliance reporting

evidence.note: Client policies require compliance to be reviewed and plans to reach targets to be outlined; the notice step is an assumption.

steps.name: Inform the board risk committee chair of a material breach
steps.description: The chief risk officer sends a short note to the chair of the board committee that oversees investment risk, ahead of the regular quarterly report, describing the breach, its cause and how it was cured or excepted.

control.basis: The model manager investment risk policy: board-approved limits on active risk, value at risk, leverage and liquidity, with breach escalation and remediation procedures: material board limit breaches reported to the board

evidence.note: Board reporting of exposures against limits; timing of the interim note is an estimate.

exceptions.name: Upstream data correction and rerun
exceptions.description: A missing price, wrong security record or position break has to be fixed by investment data management or operations and the risk calculations rerun before the report can go out.

exceptions.name: False flag from bad data
exceptions.description: A flagged limit turns out to come from a data error, which is fixed and rerun before the check is repeated.

exceptions.name: Near breach warning
exceptions.description: A measure crosses the warning threshold; the portfolio manager is told and the warning is logged.

exceptions.name: Hard breach cured by trades
exceptions.description: A board limit or client range is breached, escalated to the CIO, cured by trades and closed after the next run confirms it.

exceptions.name: Temporary exception
exceptions.description: The CIO asks for a temporary exception, for example after a private asset revaluation pushed an asset class outside its range, and the chief risk officer agrees it with an expiry date.

exceptions.name: Weekend or holiday run
exceptions.description: Results for the last business day before a weekend or holiday are reviewed on the next business day.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from market close to the published daily risk report (longer for breach follow-up)
benchmarks.population: Canadian public pension investment managers running daily risk monitoring

evidence.note: Author estimate: daily monitoring is stated by the model manager and peers; a report by mid-morning of the next business day is about 0.8 days after the close, and runs before weekends take about three days.

benchmarks.population: The national pension fund manager board reporting of risk exposures; the insurance client review of the model manager's fund risk and compliance

benchmarks.unit: confidence level of annual value at risk
benchmarks.population: AIMCo legacy public markets risk system before 2020, described as a common method of sizing active risk

evidence.note: Org file business_days driver.

pain_points.description: Most of the morning goes to data exceptions (new securities, stale prices, position breaks), so the risk team reviews the numbers late and under time pressure.

evidence.note: Common in multi-asset risk teams that buy vendor systems and feed them from several sources.

pain_points.description: Private holdings are represented by public market proxies and quarterly values, so reported risk for a large part of the portfolio is smoothed and lags.

evidence.note: Stated in the org file's process description as a known weakness.

pain_points.description: Value at risk based limits can miss non-linear and tail risks, and escalation depends on judgment, as the AIMCo VOLTS review found at a Canadian peer in 2020.
Client asset mix ranges, benchmarks and some limits live in spreadsheets maintained by hand across five client portfolios, so a stale range can cause a missed or false breach.

evidence.note: Five client policies with different ranges (org file) and common spreadsheet practice.

pain_points.description: Breach escalation waits on the availability of the CIO and chief risk officer, and the breach register is an email and spreadsheet trail.

evidence.note: Author estimate of common practice in 2019 to 2022.

sources.title: Investment Statement for the base plan and additional plan investment portfolios (February 2022)
sources.supports: Board approves market risk limits annually in equity/debt risk terms and value-at-risk terms; limits wide enough for normal daily variation; variation outside limits needs prior Board approval, with de minimis variances approved by the CEO; management monitors market, credit, liquidity and leverage risks daily; risk exposures reported to the Board at least quarterly; breach treatment and escalation set out in the Risk Policy.

sources.title: The national pension fund manager F2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Daily aggregation of risk, factor, currency and geographic exposures with trades when exposures diverge from targets; risk group independently measures and monitors key risks and reports to the Board and a management risk committee; a management risk limit standard cascades Board limits to investment departments; a new risk limits framework with systematic and timely calculation of measures.

sources.title: Alternative Assets and Risk Management: Insights into Practices Observed from FSRA's Review of Six Large Public Sector Pension Plans in Ontario
sources.publisher: Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario
sources.supports: Centralised risk control team separate from the investment team with an independent channel to senior management and the board; three lines of defence; a range of acceptable risk levels; liquidity management process; stress testing on an ongoing basis.

sources.title: The insurance client Pension Fund Statement of Investment Policies and Procedures, effective January 1, 2019
sources.supports: Client policy managed by the model manager: risk measured with total portfolio risk (standard deviation), active risk (tracking error), sensitivity analysis and factor decomposition; deviations from the policy asset mix addressed through a rebalancing policy; concentration limits.

sources.title: Insurance fund: statement of investment policies and procedures (The insurance client web page)
sources.supports: Performance, risk and compliance reviewed against objectives and the policy asset mix at least quarterly; liquidity coverage monitored at least monthly; minimum, target and maximum allocations per asset class; the model manager sets relative return and risk targets for its strategies.

sources.title: Statement of Investment Policies and Procedures for the Public Service Pension Plan (approved December 3, 2025)
sources.supports: Asset class targets with minimum and maximum ranges that the model manager must follow; private asset deviations are not violations but require a plan to reach targets; the model manager's risk discipline keeps portfolio risk close to the volatility implied by the strategic asset mix.

sources.title: Our Commitment to Client Success (The model manager web page)
sources.supports: The model manager's dedicated risk team monitors portfolios daily against target asset allocations and defined risk tolerances.

sources.title: VOLTS Investment Strategy Review: Summary of Results (AIMCo Board of Directors, June 30, 2020)
sources.publisher: Alberta Investment Management Corporation (copy hosted by Simon Fraser University)
sources.supports: A Canadian public sector manager's risk system measured active risk as 95% value at risk, which missed non-linear tail risk; escalation of risk analytics to senior management and the board was incomplete and late; the board required reporting of exposures against all limits and an escalation and remediation procedure.

sources.title: BarraOne (MSCI product page)
sources.supports: Vendor multi-asset risk system: factor risk models across public and private assets and derivatives, value at risk, full revaluation stress tests and automated risk reporting workflows.

sources.title: Wages: Financial Analyst (NOC 11101) in the Toronto Region
sources.supports: Toronto hourly wages for NOC 11101: low 27.97, median 41.60, high 73.57 (reference period 2023-2024).

assumptions: The unit of work is one business day's run covering all pools and client portfolios; touch minutes are the team's total work on that run, not per portfolio.
Daily pre-trade and post-trade guideline compliance is a separate process (investment compliance monitoring) and is not modelled here; this workflow covers risk measures and client asset mix ranges.

Per day, about 28% of runs show a warning or limit flag and about 7% end in a confirmed breach of a board limit or client range; these rates are estimates for nine pools and portfolios with dozens of limits.
The overnight batch starts four to nine hours after the book of record closes, and the morning analyst starts about six to nine hours after the batch; the weekend hold covers about one run in five.
Breach follow-up (CIO decision, trades, cure confirmation, notifications) is counted in the run's cycle time, so the 90th percentile reflects weekend runs and the few breach days.

The chief risk officer, not the board, approves temporary exceptions for management-level limits; exceptions to board limits would need board approval as in peer policies, which is rarer and not modelled separately.
Loaded costs per hour are taken unchanged from the org file (wage plus variable pay times a 1.35 loading).

The insurance client and the pension client policies cited for client ranges include versions dated after 2022; the insurance client 2019 policy shows the same kind of risk measures were in force in the reference period.
